problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=6{x}^{2}-y+{z}^{3}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes  through the point where $(x,y,z)=(\frac{1}{2},3,2).$

feedback.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=xyz-{z}^{2}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes  through the point where $(x,y,z)=(2,3,1).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(2,3,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xyz-{z}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz-{z}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(xyz-{z}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =yz\text{ }i+xz\text{ }j+(xy-2z)k \\ ∇\,f(2,3,1) & =(3)(1)\text{ }i+2(1)\text{ }j+(2(3)-2(1))k \\  & =3\,i+2\,j+4k \\  & =⟨3,2,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(2,3,1)\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-3,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨3,2,4⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-3,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ 3(x-2)+2(y-3)+4(z-1) & =0 \\ 3x+2y+4z-16 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
